steps.text: As far as she was concerned, she's always lived life the exact same way. But, to other people—
She was just like a Siracusan.
Was she just like a Siracusan?
She didn't know.
All she remembers is what she once said to her grandfather:
'People who keep going on and on about how life in Siracusa is nobler, or about life in Columbia is nobler, are all full of it.'
To which he laughed heartily.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The high-profile case of Ministro Carracci's assassination is about to be heard in court.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But it seems that only a small number of invitees are being allowed inside the courtroom, for security reasons.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Everyone else is waiting around the rione della giustizia for the outcome of the trial.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The courthouse is encircled by guards, but nevertheless, a large crowd has formed.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: It appears the death of Ministro Carracci has touched the hearts of the citizenry.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: We will continue to report on this situation as it develops, so stay tuned.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Sora, are you ready?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: You two can go, if you want, while I'm performing.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: That's alright. Even if we showed up, it's not like we'd be able to get in.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Yeah, all we can do is sit tight and wait for the verdict.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: And you break a leg out there.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Don't worry about me. I'm already in the right headspace.

steps.name: Actress
steps.text: Sora, are you ready? Almost time for curtain.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Be right there!
Volsinii Courthouse

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Quiet, please. Court is now in session.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The outcome of today's trial will be made public to all citizens of Volsinii.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The case being heard today is the assassination of Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici, Carracci.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Bring the defendant to the stand.

steps.name: Curious Spectator
steps.text: So... that's Texas?

steps.name: Noisy Spectator
steps.text: Look at the color of her eyes and hair. There's no mistaking it! She's a Texas!

steps.name: Curious Spectator
steps.text: How is she still alive?

steps.name: Noisy Spectator
steps.text: She murdered Carracci?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Silence!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Cellinia Texas, you were present at the murder of Ministro Carracci.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I was.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I planted the bomb and detonated it as il Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici was walking by.

steps.name: Curious Spectator
steps.text: She straight up admitted it?!

steps.name: Noisy Spectator
steps.text: This is the last Texas...? How the mighty have fallen!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: What was your motive?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I had none.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Who gave you the order?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No one.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: In other words, you acted alone?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Critical Juror
steps.text: Impossible! How'd you get your hands on a bomb, and when did you have the opportunity to plant it?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Does that matter?

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: Did you come to take revenge for Famiglia Texas?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Your Honor, I've confessed to everything.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I believe there's no need for these two mafiosi in the juror's box to be so rowdy.

steps.name: Critical Juror
steps.text: How dare you!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Can we just skip all the boring procedures?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Leon, what are you still doing here?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I thought you'd be at the courthouse.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is it really so surprising, Demetri?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Would you like a drink?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Let's skip the morning booze. I'll prepare some refreshing fruit juice for you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Get me a whiskey, the strongest we have.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And then, answer my question.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: How'd you guess?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Simple.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The attack on me and the assassination of Carracci both prove that someone wants the Dodici Famiglie at each other's throats.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And as Lavinia is a Bellone spokeswoman on the topic, she can't be allowed to find the murderer, or she would be able to bring the situation under control.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Therefore, now that Lavinia has arrested Cellinia, the other side can't let the trial proceed.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: So, what has to happen to Lavinia?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Fortunately, things didn't work out for you.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You might not have realized it yet, but she's already influenced you a great deal.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: It's making you question your decisions more and more.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: And through her influence on you, she might come to believe that she's capable of something.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I have to nip that flight of fancy in the bud.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Funny how you talk all confident-like.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Actually, Leon.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Doing this brings me no joy, or peace of mind.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I didn't want to wait to the very end to tell you the outcome and force you to accept it.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: So, it's just like you said. Fortunately, things didn't work out for me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But that didn't stop you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We can take all the time in the world settling this score.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Speaking of which, the safest option was to have Cellinia die mysteriously on the eve of the trial, but that didn't happen.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Proving... that the other side is afraid of her.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: After all, even if we set aside her being the last Texas, she's still a guest of the Don.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In other words, the only ones willing to let this opportunity slip by... are from this famiglia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Lo and behold, nobody made any attempts on Cellinia's life yesterday.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What if the other side anticipated your trap and purposefully held off?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If they're set on challenging Signora Sicilia's authority, you'd expect there to be a lot of commotion. So I did a bit of research into which famiglie have been the most active over the last couple days.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And it turns out... You, Demetri, are behind all of this.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I must admit, I did not expect Signorina Cellinia to stand trial for someone else's crime.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I figured it wouldn't make a difference whether or not she was involved in our plan, but by the looks of things, I really should have thought that part through.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Don't be too hard on yourself. If she didn't come out and say she was fine bearing the stain of this crime, I wouldn't have thought of it either.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: So in that case, you should show her your gratitude.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Of course I will. But before that, I have to ask: why, Demetri?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Isn't it obvious? I'm the traitor in the famiglia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'd be more willing to believe that everyone else is a traitor before you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If I can't trust you, then who?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Leon, what do you think about this new nomadic city?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Obviously, it's a new way of dividing up the spoils.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Whoever has the last laugh will be the big winner.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Sure, but I see it more as a testing ground for Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Let the Dodici Famiglie fight amongst each other here in the name of building a new city.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: The new generation of cubs vent their repressed violence, while the old wolves turn their eyes to a new prize.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Pretty great, huh? With Columbia's return to the fold, the stagnant cesspool that is Siracusa gets a new lease on life.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: No matter who wins in the end, it all works out for the woman at the top of Grey Hall, Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Wait, you don't mean...

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You've done a great job these past few years. You suppressed the other famiglie, and took control of il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: If things keep going that way, the Bellones will get that last laugh.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But what will it accomplish?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Our famiglia gets absolute control over the new nomadic city, and after that, it's back to business as usual.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And you want more than that. Or rather, he wants more than that?

spans.text: And you want more than that. Or rather,

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Since Grey Hall was established, since the Dodici Famiglie were prohibited from warring against one another, who has ever really been content?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We used to be hungry, unscrupulous wolves, and the struggles between our famiglie were bloody and endless.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But now, the newest generation of cubs is all nice and comfy in their shackles.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: They're used to coexisting with other famiglie. They find solutions to conflicts. They argue with each other in Grey Hall over what you call dividing up the spoils.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We never did any of that. No need to.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: So he wants to overthrow the Grey Hall?! But how?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: One individual has allowed the famiglie to act independently, but she will never permit them to violate her ironclad law. There can't be any fighting in broad daylight.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We were about to win, and only under these conditions could our sudden fall from power get the attention of the jealous famiglie.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Wolves fight. That's nature. They don't hold back at the smell of blood, no matter how domesticated they've become.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: They tear into each other, claws, fangs, and all.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: That's how we get this particular individual to step out of Grey Hall.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: And we'll all be waiting for that one moment.
'Crack.' The crisp sound of glass shattering echoes across the empty room.
The pup is unaware of the wounds caused by the splinters.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We'll get the last laugh, Leon.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: And when we do, we'll control more than just a new city. We'll have all of Siracusa.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: That's what your father, Bernardo Bellone, who single-handedly made the Bellones the most powerful of the Dodici Famiglie, wants for us.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You're wrong.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I haven't stopped you. Or I guess I should say, you still have a backup plan, right?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You knew from the very beginning that you'd be found out, so you waited here for me on purpose.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: The reason I'm here... is because I figured I had to face up to your anger.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I owe you an apology, both as your closest friend, and as your soldier.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I don't expect you to forgive me, but I at least want you to know that I didn't sleep well doing what I did.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Stop talking like you're giving a victory speech!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: ...I lost, Leon. Really.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But maybe, this is just the kind of place Siracusa is. Just maybe, the Don's ambitions were right.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Just as I was about to admit defeat, she appeared.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: A lunatic.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Tell me, Gambino. Can you guess the best way to ruin somebody's day?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Huh? Take his head clean off, right?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What do you think, Capone?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Find his friends and family. Kill 'em one by one, sit him down, and treat him to a slideshow with their pictures.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: *sigh*... That's why I always say you two will never amount to anything.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Hah, then let's hear your bright idea.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: His faith, my friends. His faith.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: You destroy his faith?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Destroy? No, how could you destroy a man's faith with your hands? That can't be done.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But you give him a gentle push, and let him watch his faith fall right out of the sky.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: And then, whoosh—

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Crash!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It shatters into a million little pieces.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: And how do you get a man to shatter his faith so easily?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh, no, no. You misunderstand me. Faith is pure and clean, but life is filthy.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: 'So easily'?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: A better question is, how could it be hard?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: So... does this have somethin' to do with us gettin' you that truck.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Hah, I get it. You're gonna run over that judge to shake Texas up, right?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Does she come across as the kind of woman who'd break down over one dead judge?

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: What are you gonna do then?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You're the Lappland who was exiled from Famiglia Saluzzo. Why are you here in Volsinii?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Wait, how'd you even get back into Siracusa?!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You know how the Bellones have a connection with Cellinia that nobody knows about? I got me a connection with the Saluzzo name that'd make you retch.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: So, you're here on their behalf?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You could say that.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: By the way, I think you should probably put the weapons you have under the table.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Dying here won't do you or your plans any good.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Let's make a deal, Bellone cub.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You want the case dismissed, don't you?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I can help with that.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Is that... what Alberto Saluzzo wants?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I'm his daughter, and I know him better than anyone.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haven't you been dying to find out exactly what I'm doing back in Siracusa?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's simple. I need her to understand...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: That Siracusa is a swamp. You don't get to just wade your way out.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: That goes for all of us.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: As such, you confess to having committed all the aforementioned acts?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I was.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Very well. I hereby proclaim that Cellinia Texas is guilty of murdering Ministro Carracci, Ministro dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I pronounce you—

steps.name: Critical Juror
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: What was that sound? Anybody else hear that?

steps.name: Critical Juror
steps.text: It's... an engine?

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: But we're in a courthouse. How could that—
For the mafiosi of yesteryear, the unspoken rules were held above all else.
Signora Sicilia placed the shackles of the law around the necks of the famiglie.
Thus, a court of law was erected in every Siracusan city.
In Siracusa, the courts stand for Grey Hall's will.
And the judges are executors of Signora Sicilia's will.
The judges inevitably find themselves controlled by the famiglie, sometimes even submitting to them. However, every judge knows there is one line that cannot be crossed—
They must prevent fights between the Dodici Famiglie.
Just as the Dodici all know their every move is always under the watchful eye of Signora Sicilia.
Thus, a delicate balance of power is established through the courts.
But now—
A declaration of contempt for Signora Sicilia.
A mockery of the very laws of Siracusa.
With an engine's roar squeezed between bouts of high-pitched laughter...
A truck rips through the wall.
And even after crashing its way inside, the engine does not stop.
As if proclaiming to others—
This is no mere accident, but rather by design.

steps.name: Critical Juror
steps.text: Aaaaaaahhh—

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: Wh-What's going on?! What's a truck doing here?!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Who's the driver? Get out of there this instant!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Heh, not bad. Now that's the face I wanted to see.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Who the hell are you?!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ah, yes. Buongiorno, signore e signori.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Allow me to introduce myself.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: My name... is Lappland Saluzzo.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Saluzzo?!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I am also...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Carracci's true assassin.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Breaking news!

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Just now, someone drove a truck into the courtroom.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The woman who carried out this jaw-dropping deed just identified herself as Lappland Saluzzo.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: And, she claims to be the one who really assassinated Carracci!

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: At present, Judge Lavinia has suspended the trial and detained this individual.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: We will continue to track the latest developments, so don't go anywhere—

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: When people no longer recognize the stench of blood as blood, it becomes a natural part of society.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: Let this be a poignant wake-up call.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: In a city where even the sewers are choked with conspiracy and spilled blood, such fascinating developments can still take place.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: O wolf with a yearning for the wilderness, you never fail to surprise.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: But will you break free of your shackles? That, I do wish to see.
Over a dozen mobsters lie on the ground, howling.
The only one still standing is a girl holding a longbow.
I never knew city wolves were this weak.
Agnese was right.
She pauses briefly, then suddenly turns to sniff the air.
It's coming from the direction of the warehouse.
Are there other wolves from the wilds in this city?
No... This is not the scent of the wilderness.
But, it's very close to it.
